title: Geometric etale stalks commute with unbounded derived tensor products
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a commutative ring, and $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Use the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the constant coefficient sheaf $A_T$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf], and the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ write $K_{\bar t}\in D(A)$ for the result of applying the exact geometric-stalk functor [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] termwise to a representing complex; here $D(A)$ is the derived category of ordinary $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived tensor on the site is the K-flat construction [def-kun-derived-tensor]; on $D(A)$ it is the total tensor of an ordinary-module K-flat resolution [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. For all $K,L\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ there is a canonical isomorphism in $D(A)$, natural in both variables,
$$
(K\otimes_{A_T}^{\mathbf L}L)_{\bar t}\ \cong\ K_{\bar t}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}L_{\bar t}.
$$
No boundedness, constructibility, finiteness of $A$, or Tor-amplitude hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0DEN, label lemma-check-K-flat-stalks, clause (1), applied to K-flat representatives of the derived tensor product at the point of the small etale site

proof.text: Write $S$ for the geometric-stalk functor. By [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], $S$ is exact on abelian sheaves. The same holds on $A_T$-modules: kernels, images and cokernels have their induced scalar actions, and the abelian stalk comparisons are $A$-linear. Thus $H^n(SC)=S H^n(C)$ for every complex, and $S$ preserves acyclicity and quasi-isomorphisms. For any $A$-module $M$, [def-kun-constant-sheaf] and [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-geometric-stalk] give $S(\underline M)=M$: in the constant presheaf all transition maps are identities, and every pointed neighbourhood maps to $(T,\bar t)$, so the constant-diagram colimit is $M$. This is the canonical constant-germ map, hence is natural and $A$-linear; in particular $S(A_T)=A$. Finally, the constant presheaf of an acyclic module complex is sectionwise acyclic, and its sheafification is acyclic by both clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact]. Therefore termwise constant sheaves carry acyclic module complexes to acyclic sheaf complexes.

source.place: Tags 03EI (lemma-sheafification-exact), 04EQ (lemma-stalk-exact-modules); geometric specialization also etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PT

proof.text: For any two complexes $C,D$ of $A_T$-modules, form the canonical comparison $S(C\otimes_{A_T}D)\cong SC\otimes_A SD$ of ordinary total tensor complexes. In degree $n$, [lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits] moves $S$ through $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}$, and clause (1) of [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] identifies each summand $S(C^p\otimes_{A_T}D^q)$ with $S(C^p)\otimes_A S(D^q)$. The colimit statement applies to module sheaves as well: its abelian comparison is $A$-linear, since each coprojection commutes with scalar multiplication; the colimit inherits the action from these coprojections. The differential convention of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is $d_C\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_D$ on a $(p,q)$ summand. Naturality of the ordinary tensor comparison identifies these two summand maps with $d_{SC}\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_{SD}$. The degreewise isomorphisms therefore form an isomorphism of complexes, natural in both chain maps. All sums are the small countable sums indexed by $p+q=n$; no total product or convergence assertion occurs.

proof.text: Let $P$ be any K-flat $A_T$-module complex, with K-flatness as in [def-pc-kflat-complex]. To test $SP$ against an arbitrary acyclic complex $E$ of ordinary $A$-modules, use Step 1 to see that $\underline E$ is acyclic. Then $P\otimes_{A_T}\underline E$ is acyclic by K-flatness (interchanging tensor factors by the signed symmetry if necessary). Its stalk is acyclic by Step 1 and is $SP\otimes_A E$ by Step 2 and $S\underline E=E$. This is precisely the test in [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], so $SP$ is K-flat. This constant-coefficient argument works for every acyclic $E$, without requiring boundedness or termwise flatness of $P$.

source.place: Tag 0DEN (lemma-check-K-flat-stalks), clause (1); elementary constant-coefficient proof using Steps 1 and 2

proof.text: Choose complexes $C,D$ representing $K,L$, and K-flat resolutions $P\to C$, $Q\to D$ supplied by [lem-kun-flat-resolution-existence]. We may use $P,Q$ as the representing complexes themselves, so [def-kun-derived-tensor] computes $K\otimes_{A_T}^{\mathbf L}L$ by $P\otimes_{A_T}Q$ (the identity of $P$ is a K-flat resolution). Step 1 shows that $SP\to SC$ and $SQ\to SD$ are quasi-isomorphisms, and Step 3 makes $SP,SQ$ K-flat. Thus these are K-flat representatives of $K_{\bar t},L_{\bar t}$ in the sense of [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], and their total tensor $SP\otimes_A SQ$ computes the right side. Localizing the chain isomorphism of Step 2 for $(P,Q)$ gives the asserted isomorphism. The left side is computed by $S(P\otimes_{A_T}Q)$ because the derived stalk is termwise exact.

The isomorphism is canonical and natural after localization. On K-flat representatives its comparison is exactly the chain isomorphism of Step 2, which commutes with both chain maps. Changing the first K-flat model along a quasi-isomorphism gives an isomorphism of tensor complexes in the derived category by [lem-kun-derived-tensor-well-defined]; its stalk is again a quasi-isomorphism by Step 1. Use the two K-flat representatives from Step 4. On the module side the other fixed factor is then K-flat by Step 3, so its tensor functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms by [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]; the same applies when changing the second representative. On the site side the assertion for the second factor is again [lem-kun-derived-tensor-well-defined], with the factors interchanged. The computation of both bifunctors is [def-kun-derived-tensor]. The naturality squares of Step 2 therefore remain commuting squares when any such quasi-isomorphism is inverted. The canonical independence of the K-flat construction in [lem-kun-derived-tensor-well-defined], together with the localization description [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], identifies the comparisons from different resolutions: chain-map naturality extends to inverses and composites, which generate the localized morphisms. Hence the comparison is a natural isomorphism of the stated bifunctors. No step used a bound on the complexes, a finiteness assumption on $A$, or a Tor-amplitude assumption.
